football_evidence.question: Can Kansas State contain Arizona State’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Kansas State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 4.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Arizona State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Arizona State’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.6% of its dropbacks, and Kansas State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Kansas State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Kansas State’s offense has allowed a sack on 1.5% of its dropbacks, and Arizona State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Kansas State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Kansas State’s offense averages 6.6 yards per carry, and Arizona State’s defense allows 5.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Kansas State has the ball (third down): Kansas State’s offense converts 53.5% of its third downs, and Arizona State’s defense allows opponents to convert 42.3% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).
contradicting: When Arizona State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Arizona State’s offense turns 10.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Kansas State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Arizona State’s receivers No. 25 nationally and Kansas State’s No. 64.

When Kansas State has the ball (big plays through the air): Kansas State’s offense turns 9.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Arizona State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).
quarterbacks: Cutter Boley has completed 103 of 167 passes (61.7%) for 1,353 yards, 8.1 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for Arizona State, and has been sacked on 10 of 177 dropbacks.
Mikey Keene has completed 29 of 41 passes (70.7%) for 288 yards, 7.0 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for Arizona State, and has been sacked on 4 of 45 dropbacks.

Avery Johnson has completed 119 of 188 passes (63.3%) for 1,318 yards, 7.0 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Kansas State, and has been sacked on 3 of 191 dropbacks.
